From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@acme-analytics.com>, Tom Williams <tom.williams@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 30, 2026 at 3:02 PM PDT
Subject: Discovery recap: Tool/Function-calling & Structured Output (JSON schema) — Redwood <> Acme Analytics

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps below so we’re all aligned.

Pain points you called out
- Inconsistent structured outputs from current LLM pipelines (JSON fields missing or malformed).
- Need deterministic, machine-parseable responses for downstream ingestion (analytics & rule engines).
- Tool/function invocation reliability: actions sometimes mis-invoked or missing contextual auth.
- Limited visibility/audit for tool calls for compliance.

Current stack (what you shared)
- Orchestration: homegrown orchestration with LangChain-style agents running on AWS Fargate.
- Models: mix of OpenAI and self-hosted open models; batch inference happens in separate jobs.
- Connectors: internal APIs for data enrichment and a handful of microservices for actions.

Success criteria you want for a pilot
- Deterministic JSON output that validates against a provided schema (zero-tolerance for invalid JSON).
- Clear semantics for tool calls (structured call format + signed auth headers) and at-least-once execution semantics.
- Latency target: structured response < 300ms 95th pct for typical prompt sizes.
- Auditability: request/response logging and per-call trace ids for compliance.
- Simple rollout path: start with a small set of agent workflows and expand.

What Redwood can demo/offer next
- JSON schema enforcement and a validation step in the response pipeline. Attached is a starting schema (proposed-MAP-3_0.json) based on our notes.
- Tool calling primitives with explicit call envelopes, auth token passthrough, and retry/fallback policies.
- Observability: per-request token/latency breakdown and trace ids surfaced in the Console.

Next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with your engineering team to walk the schema and tool integration (proposed owners: Marissa and Vivek).
2) We’ll prepare an acceptance test set (sample prompts + expected outputs).
3) Pilot scope: 2 agent workflows, schema validation, and audit logs for 30 days.

Proposed meeting slots: Wed 7/7 9:00 AM PT or Thu 7/8 10:00 AM PT — which works for you?

Attachments: proposed-MAP-3_0.json (sample schema)

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Patel <sara@acme-analytics.com>

Cc: Tom Williams <tom.williams@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 30, 2026 at 3:42 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Tool/Function-calling & Structured Output (JSON schema) — Redwood <> Acme Analytics

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. This matches our notes and we’re excited about the pilot. A few clarifying Qs before we lock the deep-dive: 

1) Error handling: if an agent returns invalid JSON or a tool call fails, what fallback semantics do you recommend (retry, noop, human review)? We need a safe default for production flows.
2) Fallback models/behavior: do you support a deterministic formatter step or a strict schema-enforced rejection with a structured error payload?
3) Latency: can you share typical end-to-end numbers for structured outputs (we often need <300ms 95th as Jordan noted).

We can make Wed 7/7 9:00 AM PT work for a 45–60 minute technical deep-dive — engineer attendees: myself (Sara), Tom (platform), and one of our infra engineers (TBD). I’ve attached a small example file that shows the expected output shape and a couple of edge cases (example-expected-output.json).

If you can confirm the agenda for the deep-dive and who from Redwood will present each block that’d be great.

—Sara
Product & Platform
Acme Analytics
